notice: Ten designed lifecycle journeys; no real incident, tool execution, measurement, change, or passing test is claimed. Names are reserved examples. These are not v0.1 runtime fixtures.
shared_contract: Workflow states are separate from the existing four scoped diagnosis states. Human or external owners perform any action under their own authority; this research authorizes no changes or external messages. Budget, provenance, same affected vantage and identity, verification, stabilization, non-success exits and reopen rules follow closed-loop-workflow-proposal.md. An independently documented recovery without a known action can proceed through the same original-flow verification and stabilization gates; do not invent an action or cause. Insufficient evidence remains unresolved.

cases.title: DNS resolver versus CDN steering
cases.starting_input: A user on an office client reports slow shop.example checkout with a specified resolver.

ordered_stages.design: Scope the client, checkout account, resolver, proxy, family and approved comparable endpoint; record baseline and source of topology.
Compare permitted resolver answers and timing, and hostname-preserving normal versus pinned requests to a common approved IP; retain TLS validation and actual IP.
Delayed lookup on matched repeated requests supports a resolver-stage direction; different CDN IPs with matched-IP request parity support steering as a possibility, not resolver CPU causation.

Only if evidence supports a misconfigured local resolver and its owner agrees, propose a reviewed resolver correction with backup, preconditions, rollback and operator action record; otherwise draft owner handoff.
Repeat checkout on the original client/account and path, compare agreed SLI and monitor the owner-defined window; if no matching endpoint or vantage exists, remain unresolved.

allowed_terminal_outcomes.closed_recovered: Only after recorded action or independently documented recovery, original affected vantage and same application flow/identity pass, and owner-defined stabilization coverage and SLI pass. Root-cause certainty remains separate.
allowed_terminal_outcomes.closed_unresolved: Use for an administrative handoff or reasoned stop when service recovery cannot be established; retain owner, next step, uncertainty and evidence.
allowed_terminal_outcomes.cancelled: Record cancellation, actor, pending work and any unknown external action outcome; it is not recovery.

cases.negative_control_and_local_test_design: Local two-resolver HTTPS lab independently delays DNS or HTTP; same-IP negative control prevents attributing CDN selection to resolver processing.

cases.title: Address family and split VPN
cases.starting_input: A remote user reports application failures while VPN is connected.

ordered_stages.design: Capture client, account, app operation, VPN profile and authorized routes, resolver, proxy and actual IPv4/IPv6 use; map affected and unaffected scopes.
Compare permitted matched application attempts on the actual VPN path and each family, with timestamps, identities and route evidence; distinguish VPN bypass from a comparable path.
Family-specific failure suggests a family/path direction; both fail on VPN while authorized non-VPN control works suggests VPN policy or path, not a proven device defect.

If a documented route or DNS policy mismatch is confirmed, propose owner-reviewed profile correction and rollback; otherwise hand off to VPN owner. A family workaround is mitigation, not repair proof.

After recorded owner action, repeat same operation from original VPN client and identity with the originally affected family and agreed monitoring; if route or family differs, record limits and stay unresolved.

cases.title: PPPoE and path MTU
cases.starting_input: A subscriber reports small requests work but larger uploads stall over PPPoE.

ordered_stages.design: Record CPE, subscriber session identifier with redaction, original upload and identity, link/tunnel path and owner; inspect permitted existing CPE/BNG session and interface evidence.
Compare bounded size-sensitive transfer evidence and authorized PMTU indications with a small control, recording family, encapsulation and ICMP visibility.
Size-dependent failure with consistent path evidence supports PMTU direction; server-side failures or different routes are alternatives and missing ICMP is inconclusive.
Only with supported path evidence, ask the access owner to review tunnel MTU/MSS end to end, record proposed diff, rollback and risks; no automatic device change.
Owner records action; repeat original-sized business upload from the subscriber identity and path, then monitor agreed SLI and window; absent original vantage stays unresolved.

cases.title: Interface errors and optical field handoff
cases.starting_input: An office service intermittently fails and an access interface reports errors.

ordered_stages.design: Map affected service to both interface ends and owner from timestamped inventory, noting unknown cabling and source freshness.
Review permitted error counter deltas, resets, rates, link state and module diagnostics at both ends; record units, device-reported vendor thresholds and timestamps.
Correlated error growth and optical evidence support physical investigation; an optic alert alone does not locate a break or prove a specific component defective.
Draft field-owner handoff with port IDs, observations, access constraints and requested inspection. Do not prescribe replacement until that owner validates it; no remote configuration change.

After a recorded justified repair or independently documented recovery without a known action, verify the original client application operation and account, path/family where relevant, and error-counter behavior; monitor the agreed SLI and stability window. Inaccessible client, inadequate evidence, failed checks or incomplete coverage remain unresolved.

cases.title: BGP route leak and routing owner
cases.starting_input: A branch reports loss of an external business application and a route appears unexpected.

ordered_stages.design: Record affected prefix/service, branch vantage, ASN/VRF, intended policy, owner, topology gaps and observation time.
Compare permitted route and peer snapshots to approved policy and independent observations; use optional offline modeled differential analysis only with declared snapshot limitations.
An unexpected route consistent with a leak supports routing-owner investigation; incomplete views do not prove origin, responsibility or worldwide impact.
Draft a routing-owner handoff with affected prefixes, evidence, time, uncertainty and requested policy review; no BGP change by the Skill.

After a recorded justified owner action or independently documented recovery without a known action, verify the original branch application operation and account, path/family where relevant and routes, then monitor the agreed SLI and stability window. An inaccessible original path, inadequate evidence, failed checks or incomplete coverage remain unresolved.

cases.title: Receiver zero window
cases.starting_input: A client reports that a specific upload intermittently stalls.

ordered_stages.design: Record original sender/receiver, identity, application operation, time and authorized capture location; document capture loss and encryption visibility.
Inspect bounded offline TCP evidence for advertised zero window and reopening with frame references; correlate permitted receiver socket or application data and unaffected flow.
A receiver-advertised zero window is capture-scoped evidence of receive-side flow control, not proof of the specific receiver process or a network link failure.
If receiver owner corroborates an application bottleneck, propose their reviewed mitigation and rollback; otherwise hand off receiver evidence and avoid network tuning.
After owner records action, repeat same business upload from the original client/account and monitor application SLI; capture indicators alone cannot close recovery.

cases.title: Upload queueing in a controlled lab
cases.starting_input: A user reports interactive requests slow during heavy upload.

ordered_stages.design: Define original interactive operation, client and workload; a separate consenting isolated lab owns traffic endpoints and hard bandwidth, duration and concurrency caps.
Only in the authorized lab compare idle, load and recovery windows with queue and interface evidence and same interactive flow; record independent load effectiveness and cleanup.
Repeated load-correlated latency supports queueing direction, not proof of a particular buffer or production root cause; compare host and server saturation alternatives.
If production evidence and service owner justify it, propose owner-reviewed shaping or queue policy with diff, rollback and side effects; a lab finding alone triggers investigation, not change.
After authorized human action, verify original business flow under representative permitted workload and monitor agreed SLI; if representative load is unavailable, remain unresolved.

cases.title: Intermittent failure and failed verification
cases.starting_input: Users report intermittent checkout failures; a short initial observation is successful.

ordered_stages.design: Preserve historical complaint, affected accounts, occurrence windows, prior changes and baseline; initial limited success may be not_reproduced, not permanent health.
Collect repeated permitted time-window evidence under budget and distinguish data gaps; compare a stable control and original operation.
Only if later correlated change evidence supports a candidate should an operator propose a reversible mitigation; without it continue observation or hand off unresolved.

Record owner action, preconditions, backup and rollback trigger. If original checkout fails again during verification or stability window, record failure and request owner rollback; no automatic retry.
After recorded rollback, verify original business flow and rollback state. If failure persists, action outcome is unknown or vantage is missing, hand off unresolved and reopen on new evidence.

cases.title: PPPoE discovery versus authentication
cases.starting_input: A subscriber cannot start a broadband session.

ordered_stages.design: Identify redacted subscriber/session, CPE and BNG owner, onset and intended access path; check existing local link/addressing and authorized records.

Read available CPE/BNG session state and AAA events with times and provenance; distinguish discovery with no session from established session with explicit authentication reject, and absent logs from either.
Discovery failure suggests an access path direction; a recorded authentication reject supports AAA owner investigation, without guessing credentials or billing cause.
Draft a targeted access or AAA owner handoff with evidence and unknowns; no credential reset, debug toggle, broad scan or device change.

If the owner records a justified action, check the original subscriber session and original application/account, then agreed stability. A session alone is insufficient for closure; unavailable user means unresolved.

cases.title: DHCP, default gateway and local link
cases.starting_input: An office client cannot reach its business application.

ordered_stages.design: Record affected client/interface/VLAN, business operation and account, lease age, local topology and ownership; inspect existing read-only address, default route and ARP/ND state before DNS.
Compare permitted lease and gateway-neighbor evidence with a same-segment authorized control and local link counters; retain timestamps and unknown VLAN or stale inventory.
Missing address, absent gateway or unresolved neighbor narrows the local access direction but does not prove a DHCP server or switch fault; DNS diagnosis requires usable local path evidence.
Hand off evidence to the access owner; only when a specific mismatch is independently confirmed propose their reviewed correction, backup and rollback.
After recorded action verify lease/neighbor plus the original client/account business flow and monitor the owner-defined SLI; a gateway ping alone is insufficient.
